result_1.name: JANUS Witness Quorum Intersection Gate
result_1.statement: With n witnesses, at most f Byzantine, honest witnesses refusing to certify conflicting heads at the same position, two conflicting q-witness certificates are impossible exactly when 2q>n+f; equivalently q>=floor((n+f)/2)+1.
result_1.novelty_boundary: Established quorum-intersection/BFT mathematics; not claimed as new. JANUS uses it to distribute the freshness trust root of real-world causal experiments.

result_2.name: Majority Is Not Sufficient Under Byzantine Overlap
result_2.example: n=7,f=2,q=4 is a numerical majority but unsafe: conflicting certificates {0,1,2,3} and {0,1,4,5} can coexist if witnesses 0 and 1 are Byzantine. q=5 is safe.
result_2.implication: The external bench must use a fault-model-derived quorum, not an informal majority.

result_3.name: Rollback/Fork Quorum Corollary
result_3.statement: The same honest-intersection condition that blocks two conflicting certified heads also blocks acceptance of a stale/conflicting certified rollback after a newer q-certified head, provided honest witnesses retain latest-state memory outside the experiment rollback domain.

result_4.name: Safety/Liveness Feasibility
result_4.statement: If up to a witnesses may be offline, progress requires q<=n-a, while safety requires q>=floor((n+f)/2)+1. Both are feasible exactly when floor((n+f)/2)+1<=n-a.

recommended_external_bench_baseline.fault_model: up to one Byzantine witness failure domain
recommended_external_bench_baseline.note: The four witnesses must be genuinely distinct failure domains; four processes on one rollbackable host do not count as four independent witnesses.
